title: Pre-announcement of the first Joint Transnational Call of the RCH Partnership
content:
PRE-ANNOUNCEMENT OF
Foundations for climate-resilient cultural heritage: Assessing and managing impact and risk, dealing with damage and loss

The European Partnership RESILIENT CULTURAL HERITAGE announces the 1st Call for joint research and innovation projects with an indicative total public funding of over EUR 27 million. Projects are due to commence as from December 2027.

Call opening: October 26th 2026 (indicative)
Deadline for pre-proposal submissions: January 11th 2027 (indicative)


The Resilient Cultural Heritage (RCH) initiative has been established as a co-funded European partnership, bringing together 34 funding organisations from 30 countries. The partnership is co-funded under Horizon Europe, the R&I programme of the European Union. The partners have agreed to launch the first Joint Transnational Call (JTC) 2027, aimed at collaborative and innovative research projects designed to strengthen societal resilience through cultural heritage in Europe and beyond.
This first Joint Call, involving 28 funders, is intentionally broad in terms of the range of issues addressed . The following sub-themes are included:

title: Major Cultural Heritage and Climate Change Initiative Launched in Marseille
content:
Marseille, France, 7th October 2026 — The European Partnership for Resilient Cultural Heritage (RCH), a major new initiative co-funded by the European Union, officially launched on 29 September 2026 in Marseille. The hybrid event, hosted by the Musée des civilisations de l’Europe et de la Méditerranée (MUCEM) and the Aix Marseille University (AMU), brought together more than 300 researchers, heritage professionals, policymakers and representatives of European and international organisations in person, with over 1,000 joining online. 

As climate change threatens cultural heritage worldwide through extreme weather events and rising sea levels, the launch comes at a critical time. It marks the beginning of an ambitious ten-year initiative bringing together more than 90 partners from 30 countries in Europe and beyond to strengthen research and collaboration at the intersection of cultural heritage and climate change. 

Glenn Micallef, European Commissioner for Intergenerational Fairness, Youth, Culture and Sport, welcomed the launch in a video message to attendees.

title: State of Culture Barometer 2026
content:
As Culture Action Europe prepares the second edition of our flagship publication, the State of Culture Report, we want to hear directly from those shaping the cultural and creative sectors today. Whether you are an artist, cultural manager, producer, curator, or director, working across architecture, audiovisual, crafts, design, fashion, heritage, literature, music, performing arts, visual arts, or another creative sector — your perspective matters. We are seeking voices of professionals based in the EU and candidate countries, however, responses from other countries are also valuable for certain aspects of our research.

The State of Culture Report is a biannual publication that examines the key challenges and opportunities facing the cultural sector in Europe, and how culture’s role and value are understood in national and European policies. It aims to spark critical reflection on where we stand today — and where we are heading — while contributing fresh insights to cultural advocacy and policy debates.

title: The sixth Cultural Deal for Europe policy conversation calls for culture and civil society to shape Europe’s future strategic agenda
content:
The sixth edition of the annual Cultural Deal for Europe Policy Conversation, entitled “When Culture Wins, Europe Wins”, took place on 3 February 2026 at BOZAR in Brussels, bringing together over 250 participants — policymakers, representatives of civil society, and cultural and heritage stakeholders from across Europe. The event reaffirmed the essential role of culture and cultural heritage in shaping Europe’s future, particularly in relation to democracy, social cohesion, resilience and long-term strategic priorities.

Co-organised by Europa Nostra, Culture Action Europe, and the European Cultural Foundation, the three founding partners of the Cultural Deal for Europe, the event continued the campaign’s call to place culture and heritage at the core of EU policies, to ensure the effective implementation of the Culture Compass for Europe, and to secure adequate and sustainable investment in culture — including the allocation of at least 2% of the EU budget in the next Multiannual Financial Framework (2028-2034).

title: Help Shape the Future of Burial Heritage: Contribute to the EXCALIBUR Survey
content:
Across Europe and beyond, burial sites and funerary landscapes represent some of the most sensitive and complex forms of cultural heritage. From archaeological excavation to digital documentation and ethical interpretation, professionals working in this field face unique challenges—ones that require innovative, well-informed solutions.

The EXCALIBUR Project, part of the European ECHOES EU initiative, is developing a new generation of open digital tools to support the study, preservation, and restoration of burial cultural heritage.

To ensure these tools truly respond to real-world needs, the project is inviting professionals to directly contribute to their design.

The survey is open to:

  • Archaeologists
  • Anthropologists
  • Digital humanities specialists
  • Cultural heritage professionals working with burial sites and funerary contexts

    • Whether you work in research, fieldwork, conservation, or digital innovation, your expertise is essential.

    The EXCALIBUR team is committed to a user-driven approach. Insights gathered through this survey will directly influence:

  • The design and functionality of digital tools
  • Their usability in real professional contexts
  • The priorities for future development

title: Call for expressions of interest: First Forum on Land Commons
content:
Do you collectively manage forests, pastures, water or irrigation networks, swamps, ponds, ovens or other buildings?

Everywhere in France, village communities are keeping alive shared resources, passed down from generation to generation. In 2026, these practices and knowledge will be honored at a Forum in Paris, at the UNESCO headquarters. This meeting aims to recognize land commons as contemporary systems of territorial governance, social cohesion and intergenerational transmission and as solution providers for the ecological transition.

This call is addressed to communities involved in the management or recovery of land commons, inviting them to participate in the development of the Forum. Whether you are a rights-holder, local elected official or member of a community (section de commune, consortage, bourgeoisie, cayolar, Union des prud’homies de pêche… amongst others, names vary from country to country), your experience matters. Come share your story, your knowledge and meet other communities living the same realities.

title: Cultural Heritage and Climate in South-Eastern Europe and the Mediterranean: A Common Agenda in the Making
content:
On May 15th and 16th, 2024, the ARCHE project convened a workshop in Ljubljana, Slovenia, bringing together high-level representatives to strengthen regional cooperation in cultural heritage. Hosted by the Slovenian Ministry of Culture, the event gathered speakers from Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Serbia, Montenegro, and Egypt, highlighting a growing commitment to aligning national strategies with a broader European agenda. The discussions focused on fostering cross-border cooperation and developing sustainable conservation practices to contribute to the future European Partnership for Resilient Cultural Heritage.

The workshop showcased an emerging regional cohesion, with a clear will to influence future European frameworks. Sessions featured key policy makers, including Špela Spanžel, Director-General of the Cultural Heritage Directorate for Slovenia’s Ministry of Culture, and ministry representatives Senka Ibrisimbegovic from Bosnia and Herzegovina and Almiran Toka from Kosovo. They discussed interministerial alignment and the positioning of culture as a strategic policy area, exploring how transnational cooperation can be expanded.

title: New European Bauhaus Prizes 2026: applications are open
content: The New European Bauhaus (NEB) Prizes celebrate innovative projects and ideas that embody NEB values—sustainability, inclusivity, and beauty. Over five editions, the competition has attracted more than 5,000 applications and awarded EUR 1.54 million to 72 winners. The Prizes inspire regions, cities, and towns to embrace NEB principles, foster youth participation, and promote intergenerational dialogue. A total of 13 winners will be awarded in 2026, including two public vote prizes, one ‘NEB Water Resilience’ special prize and two ‘NEB International prizes’ for Japan and Brazil. additionally, 14 runners-up will be recognised under the Prizes. Applications for this award are open until 17 March 2026. More info here.

title: Europa Nostra announces the 7 Most Endangered Heritage Sites in Europe for 2026
content:
Europa Nostra, the leading European heritage civil society network, has released today the list of the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2026, in the frame of its 7 Most Endangered Programme, run with the support of the European Investment Bank (EIB) Institute. Since its launch in 2013, this nomination-based programme has become a key civil society initiative dedicated to saving Europe’s heritage at risk, acting as a catalyst for mobilising expertise, halting unsuitable development, and/or ensuring public and private support, including funding, among other forms of assistance. Each case on the final list is eligible to receive an EIB Heritage Grant of €10,000 to support action towards saving it.

This is the list of the 7 Most Endangered Heritages sites in Europe* for 2026:

– Katapola Village and Ancient City of Minoa, GREECE

– Fábri Watermill, Feked, HUNGARY

– Blower Hall, Esch-sur-Alzette, LUXEMBOURG

– British Barracks at Fort Chambray, Gozo, MALTA

– Vale de Milhaços Gunpowder Factory, Seixal, PORTUGAL

– Reformed Church of Sântămăria Orlea, ROMANIA

– Weifert’s Brewery, Pančevo, SERBIA
